headline: 13 injured as JnU students and police clash in Old Dhaka
summary: The confrontation occurred at Murgitola intersection after students allegedly detained a man for stealing shoes, leading to a baton charge by police.
details: At least 13 people, including two journalists and five police personnel, were injured during a clash between Jagannath University (JnU) students and police at the Murgitola intersection in Old Dhaka.

The incident began around 1:00 am after a pair of shoes was allegedly stolen from the residence of a Law and Land Administration student. Students detained a man identified as Michael, who was reportedly seen in CCTV footage.
Tensions escalated when local residents allegedly freed Michael and assaulted the students, prompting hundreds of students to gather and surround a house where the suspects had taken shelter.

Police arrived at the scene to rescue the suspects. A confrontation broke out when students allegedly tried to prevent police from taking the suspects away, leading to a baton charge to disperse the crowd.
Among the injured are journalists Limon Islam and Apurba Roy. Limon Islam reported being struck by a police baton while taking photos and videos of the incident.
In protest, students blocked the Murgitola intersection for about an hour, disrupting traffic. Police have since detained Michael and another individual, Ashikur Rahman Ashik.

JnU Proctor Prof Nasir Uddin stated that the university would discuss the matter with senior police officials. Police officials have warned that legal action will be taken against those involved following an investigation.

headline: BNP prepares to dissolve expired committees, reorganization likely from August
summary: The Bangladesh Nationalist Party is set to overhaul its internal structure by dissolving committees whose terms have ended.
details: The Bangladesh Nationalist Party (BNP) is preparing to dissolve committees that have already expired. This move is part of a larger effort to reorganize the internal structure of the party.
The reorganization process is expected to begin in August, aiming to streamline operations and refresh leadership at various levels.
The party is currently reviewing the terms of various committees to identify which ones have officially expired and are required to be dissolved.
This strategic shift is intended to enhance the party's organizational strength and efficiency as it prepares for future political activities.
